entries.appliesTo: carriers, pharmacy benefit managers, private utilization review organizations, behavioral health administrative services organizations, and managed care entities that use an AI system for utilization review

dutySources.human-review: § 2, C.R.S. 10-16-112.7(5)(b) — 'SHALL NOT BE ISSUED SOLELY ON THE OUTPUT OF AN ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE SYSTEM WITHOUT HUMAN REVIEW AND APPROVAL OF THE DENIAL BY A LICENSED CLINICIAN, LICENSED PHYSICIAN, OR OTHER REGULATED PROFESSIONAL'
dutySources.impact-assessment: § 2, C.R.S. 10-16-112.7(3)(f) — 'THE ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE SYSTEM'S PERFORMANCE, USE, AND OUTCOMES ARE PERIODICALLY REVIEWED TO MAXIMIZE ACCURACY AND RELIABILITY'
dutySources.registration-filing: § 2, C.R.S. 10-16-112.7(4) — 'SHALL PROVIDE WRITTEN DISCLOSURES TO THE DIVISION, THE DEPARTMENT OF HUMAN SERVICES, OR THE DEPARTMENT OF HEALTH CARE POLICY AND FINANCING, AS APPLICABLE'

sources.humanReview: § 2, C.R.S. 10-16-112.7(5)(b) — 'WITHOUT HUMAN REVIEW AND APPROVAL OF THE DENIAL BY A LICENSED CLINICIAN, LICENSED PHYSICIAN, OR OTHER REGULATED PROFESSIONAL THAT IS COMPETENT TO EVALUATE THE SPECIFIC CLINICAL ISSUES INVOLVED'
sources.aiSoleBasis: § 2, C.R.S. 10-16-112.7(5)(b) — 'A CARRIER'S DENIAL OF COVERAGE BASED IN WHOLE OR IN PART ON MEDICAL NECESSITY SHALL NOT BE ISSUED SOLELY ON THE OUTPUT OF AN ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE SYSTEM'
sources.decisionsCovered: § 2, C.R.S. 10-16-112.7(2)(a)(I) — 'USES AN ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE SYSTEM FOR THE PURPOSE OF UTILIZATION REVIEW'

flags: human-review / sole-basis prohibition applies only to denials of coverage based in whole or in part on medical necessity (§ 2(5)(b)); subsections (3)-(4) apply to all utilization review, so decisionsCovered='all' is slightly lossy

§ 2(3)(e) requires the AI system to produce and retain 'DOCUMENTATION, AUDIT LOGS, AND MODEL-GOVERNANCE RECORDS' — internal recordkeeping, not published documentation, so no `documentation` duty assigned

§ 2(3)(a)-(d), (g)-(h) impose substantive operating conditions (determinations based on the individual's clinical data, no sole reliance on group data, nondiscrimination, fair and equitable application, data-use limitation, compliance of criteria/guidelines) that fit no listed duty key
§ 2(5)(a) expressly permits AI to assist with utilization review, 'INCLUDING EXPEDITED APPROVALS'
behavioral health administrative services organizations and managed care entities (Medicaid/behavioral-health payers) are also bound — quasi-public payers included under a company categorization
no penalty or enforcement provision in the text; codified in the insurance code (title 10, article 16) with disclosures to the division, but the text names no enforcer
effective January 1, 2027, subject to referendum petition (§ 4)

entries.appliesTo: carriers offering health benefit plans in the state; payers of mental or behavioral health-care services under the Colorado Medical Assistance Act or the Children's Basic Health Plan Act

sources.aiTherapyRule: § 2, C.R.S. 10-16-112.7(6)(a) — 'SHALL NOT PROVIDE COVERAGE FOR SERVICES THAT CONSTITUTE PSYCHOTHERAPY SERVICES, AS DEFINED IN SECTION 12-245-202 (14), THAT ARE PROVIDED DIRECTLY TO AN INDIVIDUAL AND THAT ARE CONDUCTED BY AN ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE SYSTEM'
sources.scope: § 2, C.R.S. 10-16-112.7(6)(a) — 'PSYCHOTHERAPY SERVICES, AS DEFINED IN SECTION 12-245-202 (14)'

flags: aiTherapyRule='ban' is lossy: the text bans coverage/payment for AI-conducted psychotherapy and binds payers (carriers, Medicaid/CHP+ payers), not providers — it does not prohibit the practice itself

§ 3 (C.R.S. 25.5-1-209) extends the same payment prohibition to payers under the Colorado Medical Assistance Act and Children's Basic Health Plan Act — public-program payers folded into a company entry per category rule

carve-outs: § 2(6)(b) nontherapeutic software tools (billing, EHR, video platforms) incident to human-provided services; § 2(6)(c) communications software enabling human supervision/consultation is not AI-conducted
no penalty or enforcement provision in the text
per rule 9, statutory-review is carried only by the first segment
